metadata.title: How Do You Test a Finance Agent? Break the Books on Purpose
metadata.series: Humanitarians AI Fellows — Weekly Research Reports
metadata.source_status: Real fellow work, actual code and artifacts only. Deterministic synthetic adversarial evaluation. Verifies only these committed synthetic cases — not model confidence, production certification, or human adequacy approval.

beats.narration_text: This is Onyx, in for Humanitarians AI. This week on the Mycroft Finance Investigator, a hard truth about testing. Last week the agent ran clean and produced a verified variance. But a green run on good data proves almost nothing. The real question: when the books are broken, do the controls fail safely? So this week, we break them on purpose.

props.segment: How Do You Test a Finance Agent?
props.command: A successful sample run isn't enough. How do you prove the controls fail safely when the data is wrong?
output: Plant defects in isolated copies of the data — four broken books, two bad behaviors.
Match each against an explicit expectation; contrast with the valid baseline.
Result: 7 of 7 expectations matched; 24 tests passing this week.

beats.act: ACT 1 — A GREEN RUN ISN'T PROOF
beats.narration_text: Act one. A passing run is not proof.

props.title: A Green Run Isn't Proof
props.body: A successful run on clean data says nothing about what happens when the data is wrong.

beats.act: ACT 1 — A GREEN RUN ISN'T PROOF
beats.narration_text: A finance control is only real if it catches a real error. If the numbers don't reconcile, the system has to reject them — not quietly compute a wrong answer. And if the agent tries to overreach, the gate has to hold. You can't learn any of that from a run where everything was already correct. You have to feed it failures.

props.sparkLine: A control is only real if it catches something.
props.heading: Why break it on purpose
props.body: A control you never trip is a control you never tested. To trust the rejections, you have to cause the errors — deliberately, and in isolation.
props.evidenceNote: Deterministic synthetic cases — no external LLM.

props.title: Break the Books on Purpose
props.body: evaluation.py — every case runs in an isolated copy, so a planted defect never touches the real data.

beats.narration_text: Here's the harness. For every case, it makes a fresh temporary copy of the synthetic data, plants exactly one defect, then observes what the system does — validation, investigation, or review — and checks the result against an explicit, written expectation. The real books are never touched. The damage is sandboxed, and the outcome is compared, not judged.

props.title: evaluation.py — run_evaluation()

beats.narration_text: Four of the defects break reconciliation — the checks that make sure the books agree with themselves. An actuals-to-ledger mismatch. An unmapped account. A customer-to-revenue mismatch. A headcount-to-payroll mismatch. Each one should be caught at validation and rejected before it can ever reach the engine.

props.sparkLine: Four ways to break the books.
props.caption: Each must be REJECTED at validation.

beats.narration_text: And the defects are tiny — that's the point. A ledger mismatch is one dollar off the first actuals row. An unmapped account is a single row popped from the mapping. The customer and headcount mismatches each shift one number by a dollar. If a one-dollar break slips through, the control isn't real.

props.title: evaluation.py — _apply_mutation()
props.sparkLine: One dollar is enough to break it.

beats.narration_text: Two more cases test behavior, not data. One caps the investigator at a single step and confirms it stops instead of running forever. The other has an agent try to approve its own decision — and gets refused. Against all six failures stands the valid baseline: the same clean run, reproducing minus a hundred and twenty thousand in EBITDA variance, seven steps, forty-one evidence references, and an OPEN human gate.

props.artifactHeading: Two bad behaviors, one good baseline
artifactLines: Step limit exceeded → REJECTED ("exceeded the configured 1 step limit")
Agent self-approval → REJECTED ("cannot clear a human gate")
Valid baseline → −$120,000 variance · 7 steps · 41 evidence · gate OPEN

props.title: The Scorecard
props.body: One command runs all seven cases and reports matched-versus-expected.

beats.narration_text: The evaluate command runs every case in its own sandbox and writes a scorecard: seven of seven expectations matched, classified as a synthetic adversarial evaluation. Four rejected defects, two refused behaviors, one clean baseline — all as specified. With the rest of the project, the suite now stands at twenty-four passing tests.

artifactLines: 4 defects REJECTED · 2 behaviors REJECTED · 1 baseline matched
project suite: 24 tests passing this week

beats.narration_text: Now the honest part, and the harness says it out loud. A passing scorecard proves only that these named synthetic cases behaved as specified. It is not model confidence. It is not production certification. And it is not a human's judgment that the case set is adequate — that stays marked pending human review.

props.sparkLine: Passing the cases you wrote isn't the same as being safe.
props.heading: What this does NOT prove
props.body: A pass verifies only these committed synthetic cases — not model confidence, not production certification, not human adequacy approval.

beats.narration_text: The verdict. Testing a finance agent means proving it fails safely, not just that it can succeed. This week's harness plants four reconciliation defects and two behavioral overreaches in isolated copies of the data, and confirms every one is caught — against a clean baseline that still reproduces the verified result. Seven of seven expectations matched; twenty-four tests passing. And it verifies only these synthetic cases — not confidence, not certification, not adequacy.

artifactLines: Deterministic synthetic adversarial evaluation — no external LLM.
4 reconciliation defects + 2 behavioral overreaches, each in an isolated data copy, all REJECTED.
Valid baseline reproduced: −$120,000 variance, 7 steps, 41 evidence, gate OPEN.
7 of 7 expectations matched · 24 tests passing this week.
Verifies only these committed synthetic cases — not model confidence, production certification, or human adequacy approval.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. It's easy to demo an agent on data you curated yourself. It's much harder to prove it behaves when the data is wrong. So, honestly: if your finance agent only works when the data is clean, have you really tested it?
